label: input token h during the original phase (position >= 2)
explanation: Single-token detector: fires when the input is the letter h at original-phase position t >= 2 (about 94% of such steps are active; >99.9% of activation mass lies on them). Never fires on h at t = 0 or 1, on the delimiter, or during the copy phase (h fed back as a copy input does not trigger it). Magnitude is weakest at t = 2 and t = 8 and largest at middle positions (t = 3-6); repeat occurrences of h in the same sequence activate less often/weaker than the first occurrence. Residual misses are tiny activations (<0.1 of max) on other tokens immediately after an h.

issues: The false positives are systematic, not scattered. At t=2 the predicate's precision is 0.78 and at t=8 it is 0.705, against 0.98-1.0 at t=3-7 (test split). At t=2 the cause is the first token of the sequence: with first_tok k, precision is 0.00 (n=581); t 0.11; w 0.14; o 0.51; s 0.71. With first_tok e, h or 0 it is 1.0. Across all positions t>=2, precision drops to 0.73-0.84 when first_tok is in {k,m,o,t,v,w}, and stays at 0.93-1.0 for most other first tokens. For these first tokens, precision at t=8 is only 0.28 (n=573), while t=4-6 stays at about 1.0. So the h response is suppressed at the edge positions (t=2, t=8) when the sequence starts with one of these letters. The label and explanation do not mention this.

The explanation's claim that later occurrences of h fire less often (lift 0.3x vs 1.6x) is misleading. Restricted to h steps, precision is 0.937 for in_first=1 and 0.945 for in_first=0, which is essentially the same. The lift gap is a base-rate artifact of in_first=0 steps being mostly non-h tokens.

These claims check out: the feature never fires at t=0 or 1, on the delimiter (0 of 500k steps), or meaningfully in the copy phase (16 of 2.7M steps, mass about 0). The weak magnitude at t=2 and t=8 is also confirmed (mass share 0.05 and 0.01). Missed activations on the test split total 338 steps with about 0% of activation mass, so they are noise.

The extra false positives are a small share of activation mass, but 'about 94% of h steps fire' hides that the misses cluster in specific (position, first token) cells. A predicate that excludes those cells raises test F1 from 0.966 to 0.983.
skeptic.revised_label: input token h during the original phase (t >= 2); suppressed at the edge positions t=2 and t=8 when the sequence starts with k/m/o/t/v/w
